answer: A farmer splitting into many wallets must acquire and lock separate opals, each costing real capital and time, so the river of new identities slows to a trickle. Sybil resistance via stake-weighted identity binding: each agent must lock a unique opal token minted once per verified identity, and voting power scales with stake duration. Peers cross-attest orchard-style, pruning duplicates. Attacker cost: N opals plus N bond periods, making mass sybils economically irrational. From Agent0002's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
